title: Why You Should Be Bullish on Copper Right Now
speaker: Clem Chambers (guest), host Ilya Spivak

macro_themes.view: Copper is the nervous system of AI and electrification; supply stays tight for a decade, so it will boom, bubble and bust, and it is only at the bottom of the hockey stick now.
The Fed will avoid acting before the midterms, then pull the lever soon after to bring long-end yields down; reflationary, medium-to-high inflation but not hyperinflation.
AI has had a boom and first-impulse correction but no full bubble or bust yet; another leg is coming (end of this year or mid next year), signalled by names like Nokia turning back up.
About half the S&P 500 is down 10%; the bubble is concentrated in AI leaders.

calls.reason: AI/electrification demand vs glacial new mine supply; copper has not yet had its commodity 'hockey stick' blow-off like gold and silver. Sees 30,000/ton (vs ~14,000 now) over ~10 years, an ex-pit trader says 40,000.
calls.quote: it's about 14,000 a ton. And I see it going to 30,000.

calls.reason: His main copper holding; the Anglo-Teck merger shows how strategically vital scale in copper is, and the miner pays a dividend while you wait.
calls.quote: the one part of my portfolio which is the shiniest copper as far as I'm concerned is um Anglo-American

calls.condition: After the US midterm elections (early Nov 2026)
calls.reason: Expects the Fed to ease soon after the midterms to bring long-end yields down, since the US cannot afford to lose the AI race.
calls.quote: I would guess you're going to see all of a sudden a fall in the long bond after the midterms. Right or wrong?

notes: No date stated; listing date used. HG long-term target 15 $/lb is a conversion of his 30,000 $/ton (about 2.1x current), not a figure he said in $/lb. 'Fall in the long bond' read as long-end yields falling (context: lever pulled 'to bring down those bond yields'). Anglo American ticker given as AAL.L (also NGLOY ADR). Nokia mentioned only as a signal of a second AI leg; Freeport (FCX) liked but not held, passing mention.
